subject: maths
title: Area of composite shapes and sectors

scenes.heading: Area of composite shapes and sectors
scenes.sub: Add the pieces, subtract the holes
scenes.say: How much grass is in a lawn with a curved end? Or how much paving goes around a round pond? Today you'll find areas of slices of circles and of shapes built from simple pieces.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Dough left = sheet minus the biscuits you cut out
scenes.science: Composite area: add joined pieces, subtract cut-out pieces
scenes.breaks: Real dough stretches and can be re-rolled; maths shapes never change size.
scenes.say: Think about cutting biscuits from a sheet of dough. The dough left over is the sheet minus the circles you cut out. Stick two pieces together and you add them. Composite areas work the same way: add the pieces you join, subtract the pieces you cut out.

scenes.heading: Sector area
scenes.say: A sector is a slice of a circle. Its area is theta over three sixty, the fraction of the circle, times pi r squared, the area of the whole circle.
scenes.caption: A sector is a slice of a circle. Its area is θ/360 (the fraction) × πr² (the whole circle).

scenes.heading: Sector example
scenes.question: Find the area of a sector with radius 10 cm and angle 72°, to 1 decimal place.
scenes.say: Radius ten centimetres, angle seventy-two degrees. Seventy-two out of three sixty is one fifth. The whole circle is one hundred pi. One fifth of that is twenty pi, about sixty-two point eight square centimetres.
scenes.caption: 72/360 = ⅕. Whole circle = 100π. Sector = 20π ≈ 62.8 cm².

scenes.heading: Joined on: add
scenes.say: First a rectangle, ten by six. Then a semicircle joined on the end. Its diameter is six, so the radius is three. Rectangle sixty, plus half of pi times three squared, gives about seventy-four point one square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Rectangle 10 × 6 = 60. Semicircle: diameter 6, so r = 3; area = ½ × π × 3². Total ≈ 74.1 cm².

scenes.heading: Cut out: subtract
scenes.say: Here's a square with side eight. A quarter circle of radius eight is cut out of it, leaving the shaded corner. Square sixty-four, minus a quarter of pi times eight squared, leaves about thirteen point seven square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Square 8 × 8 = 64. A quarter circle, ¼ × π × 8², is cut out. Shaded ≈ 13.7 cm².

scenes.heading: Ring trap
scenes.say: For a ring, find the big circle and subtract the small circle: pi R squared minus pi r squared. Do not subtract the radii first and then square. That gives a much smaller, wrong answer.

Quick recap. Sector area is theta over three sixty times pi r squared. Semicircles are half and quadrants are a quarter. Add pieces that are joined on, subtract pieces that are cut out, and halve a diameter first. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Sector = θ/360 × πr². Semicircle ½πr², quadrant ¼πr². Joined on: add. Cut out: subtract. Halve a diameter first. Now try the practice questions!
